summary: The video side is split along MAME's taito_f3_v.cpp functions, not along the F3's custom chips (TC0630FDP/TC0650FDA/TC0640FIO). There is a line-RAM decoder that matches read_line_ram, a playfield builder that matches get_pf_scroll and the per-line part of scanline_draw, a sprite walker that matches get_sprite_info, a sprite rasterizer that matches f3_drawgfx, and a mixer that matches mix_line/render_line. Inside those modules the HDL repeats MAME's own expressions, constants, default values, layer ordering and even MAME's documented hacks. The FPGA work around them (line buffers, two fetches in flight, 9 pipeline stages per pixel) is neutral and does not offset how closely the logic follows the C++.

findings.note: The section/subsection latch addressing, the FIX_Y {0,3,2,1} y-zoom swap, blend = min(8, 0xF-alpha), x_sample = 16 - bits, fx_6400 = (v & 0xfc00)>>8, x_scale = 256 - hi byte, pal_add*16 and the rowscroll (v<<2 & ~0xff) - (v<<2 & 0xff) are all copied one for one from MAME. MAME itself marks that last expression 'allegedly'.

findings.signal: MAME line-state struct as the interface
findings.where: rtl/rf_video_line.sv ports; rtl/rf_video_pipe.sv line decoder instance
findings.note: The decoded per-line outputs use MAME's struct field names and defaults: colscroll, alt_tilemap, x_scale (default 0x80), y_scale, pal_add, rowscroll, x_sample (default 16), fx_6400, bg_palette, pivot_control, pivot_enable, plus the mix words. They are not named after the board's signals.

calc_sx adds (40-4*pf)<<6, shifts to 24.8, XORs with 0xFC and subtracts H_START<<8 (11776). calc_sy adds 1<<7 and negates under flip. The x origin is reg_sx + rowscroll + 10*(x_scale-256), and fx_y += y_scale only when screen_y != 0. These are all MAME's expressions and its 'what is with this calculation' constant.

Before building, each layer scans its tilemap or text row for non-zero codes and marks the line unused if all are zero. That mirrors MAME's software skip-if-row-empty bookkeeping, which the mixer then uses as part of layer enable. It does not come from any board mechanism.

findings.signal: mix_line layer order, sort and blend state
findings.mame_ref: taito_f3_v.cpp:scanline_draw (layers array + stable_sort), mix_line, calc_clip, render_line
findings.note: BASE_KIND {pivot, sp0, pf0, sp3, pf3, sp2, pf2, sp1, pf1} is MAME's layers[] initializer, and the rank loop reproduces std::stable_sort by prio. Each stage keeps MAME's src/dst pal, blend and prio, with src_blendmode starting at 'invalid' (MAME's 0xff). It also copies dst_pal=0 on a prio conflict, clip_l-1 / clip_r-2, and the (s*sb + d*db)>>3 clamp.

axis_np and the block_ctrl case 0/2/3 copy sprite_axis::update, including the 0b00 fallthrough into pos=block_pos and pos += block_scale*16. The walker breaks when jump target == offs, caps at total_sprites < 0x400, skips tile==0, computes (512<<8)-scale*16-pos for flip, and culls against MAME's visible_area.

The y accumulator starts at ty + 255 when not flipped (MAME's 'round up in non-flipscreen mode?'). The x dedup 'skip if the next pixel lands in the same column' (dx != dx8>>8) is copied, and the bucket order is chosen so that MAME's reverse-list write-if-empty result wins.

The pixel layer takes its palette from text-RAM row y (+32 when y*8+scroll (+0x100 if flipped) >= 256). That is MAME's comment-labelled HACK, not a board mechanism. The pivot x scroll uses MAME's -12 / -5 offsets.

findings.signal: MAME per-game config instead of a hardware register
findings.note: The extend bit and the visible-area variant come from a per-game config byte that mirrors MAME's f3_config_table and its four screen configs. They are not decoded from the video control register the game writes.
IRQ3 is a counter set to 10000 68020 cycles after the vblank IRQ2, which is MAME's timer guess. It is not derived from any board video signal.
A boot FSM copies the first 8 ROM bytes into sound RAM 0-7 before releasing the 68000. That reproduces MAME's std::copy of the stack and reset vectors, not the board's reset-time ROM/RAM mapping.

The work runs ahead of the beam in line buffers (mix T+1, build T+2), with dual sprite fetches and a pipelined mixer. These are resource-driven FPGA choices. H_TOTAL=432, H_START=46 and V_TOTAL=262 match MAME's constants, as any correct core must.
